title: TrailGuard AI cameras in the Kanha-Pench corridor transmit tiger alerts to researchers and forest officials 30 to 42 seconds after detection in a 2022 pilot
summary: BioScience 2023: 12 TrailGuard AI cameras ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh, mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights); tiger notifications arrived 30 to 42 seconds after detection.
account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers and humans and transmit only images of interest. Researchers and forest department officials received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim. The cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. The paper's second site, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers, is recorded separately. No forest department document on the pilot is among the sources.
purpose: Real-time detection of tigers and humans for human-wildlife conflict early warning and anti-poaching. The reported detections and follow-up were the intended use.
system: TrailGuard AI camera-alert system with embedded AI (Intel Myriad processor; detectors trained with CVEDIA synthetic renderings)
developer: RESOLVE (design) with CVEDIA Ltd (AI training); units manufactured by Nightjar
deployer: Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh forest departments with Clemson University, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum
segment: State forest departments and conservation research partners

ratings.reason: No identified individual beneficiary. Villagers near three units are mentioned only as sources of daily notifications.
Researchers and forest department officials received tiger alerts 30 to 42 seconds after detection during the two-month pilot. No action taken on an alert is documented.
No measured effect on human-wildlife conflict in the two-month pilot of 12 cameras.

ai_role.statement: Embedded AI on the camera selected and transmitted images of tigers and humans within 30 to 42 seconds. That is the mechanism in the developer-affiliated BioScience paper. Whether any alert changed what villagers or officials did is not documented.

later.note: AFP reported that RESOLVE's Eric Dinerstein was widening the TrailGuard rollout to larger animals such as elephants; the BioScience article also notes continued transmission from Kanha-Pench and other reserves.
later.quote: Those uncertainties aside, Dinerstein is widening the rollout of TrailGuard — this time with even bigger animals in his sights.

fields.account: Dertien et al. reported in BioScience (published 14 September 2023) that 12 TrailGuard AI camera-alert systems ran in the Kanha-Pench corridor, Madhya Pradesh. They ran from mid-May to mid-July 2022 (591 trap nights). The cameras run embedded AI on an Intel Myriad chip to detect tigers and humans and transmit only images of interest. Researchers and forest department officials received tiger notifications 30 to 42 seconds after detection. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim. The cameras were “immediately effective, picking up a tiger just 300 meters from a village”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) reported the Madhya Pradesh deployment. It quoted H.S. Negi of the Global Tiger Forum on plans to incorporate the system in other tiger reserves. The paper's second site, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh, where a unit captured armed poachers, is recorded separately. No forest department document on the pilot is among the sources.
